name: Talon 2
frame: ALUXX-grade aluminium, 12×142 mm thru-axle, internal routing
fork: SR Suntour SXC32-3 RL, coil spring, Boost 15×110 mm, lockout
brakes: Tektro HD M3121 hydraulic, 180 / 160 mm rotors
wheels: Giant alloy, double wall, tubeless compatible (27.5 in on XS and S)
description: The hardtail most riders start on: a light aluminium frame, a 100 mm fork and one chainring, so there is nothing to think about but the trail.
ride: It climbs pass roads without fuss and stays calm on loose gravel. The 2.4 in Maxxis tyres grip more than the price suggests, and the 1×9 gearing is simple to keep clean. Ride it for a season, then add a dropper post when the trails get steeper.

name: Talon 29 3
fork: SR Suntour XCE, QR, steel steerer
drivetrain: Shimano Altus 2×8 shifters, Acera rear derailleur, 11–39T, 22/36 crank
wheels: Giant GX03V 29, double wall, 21 mm inner width
description: The lowest-priced way onto a real mountain bike: hydraulic brakes, Maxxis tyres and two chainrings for the long climbs out of town.
ride: Sixteen gears make long, steady climbs easy and the hydraulic brakes are calm on wet descents. It is the bike we suggest for riders who want to try dirt roads and passes before spending more.

name: Talon 29 1
fork: SR Suntour SXC32-2 RL, air spring, 100 mm, lockout
description: An air fork you can set to your weight and a wide-range Deore 1×10: the hardtail for riders who are already out every weekend.
ride: The air fork is the difference you feel first — set it to your weight and the front end stops bouncing on rocky climbs. The 51-tooth cog gets you up the steep end of a pass seated.

name: Tempt 29 0
fork: SR Suntour SXC32-2 RL, air spring, hydraulic lockout, 100 mm
drivetrain: Shimano Deore M6100 1×12, 10–51T, KMC X12 chain
description: Liv's best-equipped hardtail, shaped for women riders: a shorter reach, narrower bar and a saddle that fits, with twelve speeds and an air fork.
ride: Riders who have struggled with a frame built for someone taller feel the difference in the first corner. Twelve speeds and a 51-tooth cog cover every climb we know.

name: Anthem X Advanced SL 3
frame: Advanced SL-grade composite, 120 mm FlexPoint Pro, in-frame storage, adjustable geometry
description: A carbon cross-country bike with a little more travel and a slacker head angle, for fast riders whose trails turn rough on the way down.
ride: It pedals like a race bike — firm, quick and light up every climb — and the extra 10 mm up front lets you stay off the brakes on rocky descents. The frame's storage hatch holds a tube and a pump.

name: Anthem Advanced SL 0
frame: Advanced SL-grade composite, 120 mm FlexPoint Pro, frame 1,530 g (M)
fork: RockShox SID Ultimate 3P, 120 mm, Charger Race Day 2, remote lockout
drivetrain: SRAM XX SL Eagle Transmission AXS 1×12, Quark power meter, 34T
wheels: Giant XCR carbon WheelSystem, carbon spokes
description: The bike of world-cup cross-country racing: a carbon frame, wireless shifting with a power meter and suspension locked from the bar.
ride: At ten kilos it climbs as if the pass were half as long. It asks for a rider who races or trains with numbers — and for the shop to set it up with you, which we do as part of the sale.

name: Pique Advanced SL SE
frame: Advanced SL-grade composite, women's race geometry, 120 mm FlexPoint Pro
fork: RockShox SID Ultimate, 120 mm, remote lockout
drivetrain: SRAM XX SL Eagle Transmission AXS 1×12
description: Liv's special-edition race bike: the lightest frame Liv makes, women's geometry, and the best parts SRAM and RockShox build.
ride: Made for one job — going uphill and through technical cross-country faster than anything else. We order each one for its rider; leave your details and we will call when the next one lands.

name: Stance 0
frame: ALUXX-grade aluminium, 130 mm FlexPoint suspension, UDH, 12×148 mm
fork: Giant STL 34 RC, dual air, 140 mm, Boost 15×110
shock: Crest FloTrac Elite, 2-position lever, trunnion mount
wheels: Giant TRA hookless alloy, 30 mm inner width (mixed 29/27.5 on XS)
tyres: Maxxis Minion DHF 29 × 2.5 in front, Dissector 29 × 2.4 in rear
description: A full-suspension trail bike at a hardtail rider's budget: 130 mm at the back, a 140 mm air fork and a modern SRAM twelve-speed.
ride: This is the bike for broken pass roads and rooty singletrack: the rear end keeps the tyre on the ground when a hardtail would skip. A 65.5° head angle makes it steady downhill without feeling heavy uphill.

name: Stance
description: Giant's entry-level dual-suspension bike, sitting between the Talon hardtail and the Trance X: 130 mm of travel and a Fox Rhythm shock.
ride: The first full-suspension bike for most of our customers. The Shimano CUES drivetrain is hard-wearing and cheap to service, and the bike is happy on everything from gravel to the steep end of a trail.

name: Trance X 1
frame: ALUXX SL aluminium, 140 mm Maestro, flip chips, in-frame storage
fork: Fox 36 Float Performance, GRIP, 150 mm, Kabolt X axle
shock: Fox Float Performance, 2-position, tuned for Giant
wheels: Giant TRA hookless alloy, 30 mm inner width
tyres: Maxxis Assegai 29 × 2.5 in front, Minion DHR II 29 × 2.4 in rear
description: Our favourite all-round trail bike: Maestro suspension, a Fox 36 and tyres that grip on wet rock, with geometry you can change with a flip chip.
ride: It climbs on the firm setting and descends like a much bigger bike. Riders who bought it for weekend trails find it handles bike-park days too. The dropper drops up to 200 mm on the large sizes.

name: Intrigue X 2
frame: ALUXX SL aluminium, 140 mm Maestro, women's suspension tune
shock: Fox Float Rhythm, tuned for lighter riders
wheels: Giant alloy, 29 in front, 27.5 in rear
tyres: Maxxis Assegai 29 × 2.5 in front, Minion DHR II 27.5 × 2.4 in rear
description: Liv's trail bike, with suspension tuned for lighter riders and a smaller rear wheel that makes it easy to move around under you.
ride: Riders under 60 kg finally get suspension that moves on small roots instead of only big hits. The mixed wheels roll over rock at the front and turn quickly at the back.

name: Talon E+ 1
frame: ALUXX aluminium e-MTB hardtail, side-release battery
fork: SR Suntour XCR 32 Air, 100 mm, lockout
motor: Giant SyncDrive Core, 60 Nm · EnergyPak 500 Wh, side release
description: An electric hardtail that makes a long pass a morning ride: a quiet Giant motor, a 500 Wh battery you lift out to charge at home.
ride: The motor adds to what your legs give, up to 25 km/h, and the battery lasts a 60–80 km day in the middle setting. Riders use it for the climbs they used to walk.

name: Tempt E+ 1
frame: ALUXX aluminium, women's e-MTB geometry, integrated battery
motor: Giant SyncDrive Core, 60 Nm · EnergyPak 500 Wh, integrated
wheels: Giant alloy, 29 in front, 27.5 in rear
description: Liv's electric hardtail for women riders, with the battery hidden in the down tube and a smaller rear wheel for easy handling.
ride: A light, low e-MTB that does not feel like a motorbike. This season's bikes have sold — leave your details and we call you when the next ones arrive.

name: Embolden E+ 0
frame: ALUXX SL aluminium, full suspension, integrated battery
motor: Giant SyncDrive Pro, 85 Nm · EnergyPak 800 Wh, integrated
tyres: Maxxis Assegai / Minion DHR II 29 × 2.5 in
description: A full-suspension electric trail bike with an 800 Wh battery — enough for a whole day in the mountains, two passes and back.
ride: The strongest motor Giant makes and a battery big enough that range stops being the question. Riders take it where they would never have pedalled a bike before.
